page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with no hyperthreading, providing 16 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and includes a 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Network performance is anchored by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, managed under the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and decompression capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression (36.48 GB/sec) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.31 GB/sec), alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 4380.5. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (257.74 GB/sec) and static web serving throughput (54.77 GB/sec) are rated as strong. Standard compute benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (2009.9) and multi-core (32099.07), fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.4xlarge leverages the ARMv9 architecture to deliver high resource density and strong memory bandwidth without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The inclusion of 950 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for database operations, which is supported by a strong PassMark database score of 29397.82. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, database hosting, data compression tasks, and medium-sized language model text generation.
